windows_intro: CowCatcher AI runs on the open-source AI Detector engine. Follow the eight steps below and your barn is being monitored live — everything runs locally on your own Windows PC, without a subscription.
windows_download_desc: Choose the correct file for your hardware in the latest release.
windows_req_title: Before you start: which version do you need?
windows_req_text: You need a computer with Windows 10 or Windows 11. Your graphics card (GPU) decides which build of the AI engine you install. All versions are fast enough for accurate detection; a NVIDIA card simply processes more frames per second.
windows_hw_win11_any: Windows 11 with any GPU (Intel HD/UHD/Iris or AMD Radeon)
windows_hw_win10_rtx3000: Windows 10 with NVIDIA RTX 3000 series or newer
windows_hw_win10_rtx2000: Windows 10 with NVIDIA GTX 1000 / RTX 2000 series or older
windows_table_web: The user interface, needed on every PC
windows_note_title: Not sure which one to choose?
windows_note_text: Start with the winml version on Windows. Only use a cuda build if you are certain that your NVIDIA setup matches that specific CUDA version.
windows_step1_title: Download the two files from GitHub
windows_step1_1: Open the releases page of the AI Detector project with the button above, or search Google for “CowCatcher AI GitHub” and click Releases in the right-hand menu.
windows_step1_2: Download exactly two files: the AI engine that matches your graphics card, and the web version (aidetector-web-windows) — the interface where you set everything up.
windows_step1_github_note: For the standard winml version you can download without an account. For the NVIDIA (CUDA) builds GitHub requires you to be signed in: go to github.com, click Sign in and choose ‘Continue with Google’ to use your existing Google account. That takes a few seconds.
windows_step1_caption: The releases page: the engine builds are listed under Assets and in the release description.
windows_step2_title: Create a folder and unpack the files
windows_step2_1: Right-click an empty spot on your desktop and choose New → Folder. Give it the clear name Cowcatcher.
windows_step2_2: Open File Explorer, go to Downloads and select both .zip files. Press Ctrl + X, open the Cowcatcher folder and press Ctrl + V.
windows_step2_3: Right-click the first zip file and choose Extract All…, then confirm. Do exactly the same for the second zip file.
windows_step2_4: Both programs are now unpacked in the folder. You can safely delete the original .zip files.
windows_step2_caption: The Cowcatcher folder with both programs unpacked: the AI engine (winml) and the web interface.
windows_step3_title: Allow Windows to run the program
windows_step3_intro: CowCatcher AI is not distributed through the Microsoft Store, so Windows shows a security warning as a precaution. Two short actions remove it for good.
windows_step3_a_1: Right-click the program (.exe) and choose Properties at the very bottom.
windows_step3_a_2: On the General tab, under Security, you see the text: “This file came from another computer and might be blocked to help protect this computer.”
windows_step3_a_3: Tick Unblock, click Apply and then OK. Do this for both programs.
windows_step3_caption: Right-click the .exe → Properties → tick ‘Unblock’ under Security and confirm with OK.
windows_step3_b_1: The first time you open the program a blue screen may appear saying “Windows protected your PC” (Windows Defender SmartScreen).
windows_step3_b_2: Click the small link More info and then the button Run anyway that appears. The program now has full permission.
windows_keep_1: Use a network cable. Connect both the AI computer and the IP cameras with a wired connection (UTP/ethernet). Wi-Fi in a barn can be unstable, which makes the RTSP streams stutter.
windows_keep_2: Switch off sleep mode. Does the AI stop detecting at night? Then Windows put the PC to sleep. Go to Settings → System → Power & sleep, set the screen to switch off after e.g. 15 minutes, but set Sleep to Never.
windows_keep_3: Start automatically after a power cut. Press Windows + R, type shell:startup and press Enter. Right-click your CowCatcher AI program, choose Create shortcut and drag that shortcut into the Startup folder that just opened. The program now starts by itself whenever the computer boots.
